summary: AE + SE demo of Redwood structured output (JSON mode) and function/tool-calling features for Acme Retail. Walked through schema validation, guardrails, Console mapping, API examples and POC plan. Customer raised latency/cost questions and enterprise security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to POC with structured testset and follow-ups to share pricing and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood - i own this account. we also have Priya (SE) on the line to do a deep dive demo.
[00:00:10] Tom: hey Alex, thanks. Tom here, CTO at Acme. we've got Maya our ML lead and Samir on infra.
[00:00:18] Alex: awesome, quick agenda: short intro, demo of structured output + function calling in JSON mode, then Q&A and POC next steps. sound good?
[00:00:26] Maya: yep good. we're primarily interested in using the structured output to drive downstream inventory update calls and fraud scoring via tools.
[00:00:34] Priya: perfect, i'll share my screen — starting with the API examples. Redwood supports a JSON mode where you pass a schema and the model returns a validated JSON object; we also demonstrate function-calling so you can hook up an internal tool to consume that object.
[00:00:47] [00:00:47] Speaker 1: (screen noise) 
[00:00:50] Priya: first example: prompt -> schema for order-update: fields: order_id, items[], quantities, reason_code. we show how the runtime will enforce type checks and optional fallback when the model outputs malformed text.
[00:01:05] Maya: do you validate on the service side or is it client-side? like who enforces the schema?
[00:01:12] Priya: good question — Redwood offers server-side schema validation as part of the structured-output endpoint. you provide a JSON schema; the service will attempt to coerce and validate the model output, and if it fails, Redwood can either return an error, run a repair prompt, or fall back to a safe function that asks for clarification.
[00:01:28] Tom: ok so that helps reduce parsing errors downstream. can you show an example where the model hallucinates a field and how you handle it?
[00:01:35] Priya: sure — demo: prompt says 'extract order info from message' — model sometimes invents 'promo_code' — the schema doesn't include promo_code so Redwood strips unexpected keys and logs them. you can configure an allow-list or map unknown fields to metadata.
[00:01:52] [00:01:52] Alex: log visibility is in the Console — you can see per-request token usage, latency and any schema mismatches in the trace.
[00:02:00] Samir: how frequent are those repairs? like if we send high QPS, does repair add a lot to latency?
[00:02:07] Priya: repairs can add a round trip depending on the strategy. two modes: synchronous repair (extra model call) or async review (write to a queue). for low-latency paths we recommend strict schema + function fallback to ask the upstream system to verify rather than another LM call.
[00:02:22] Maya: can we see the function-calling glue? that's the important bit for integrating with our inventory service.
[00:02:27] Priya: yep — switching to function calling tab. here we define a function signature: updateInventory(order_id:string, items:array[itemId,qty], warehouse:string). Redwood can invoke your service directly via webhooks or via an internal connector in Dedicated/Private deployments.
[00:02:44] [00:02:44] Speaker 2: background noise 
[00:02:46] Priya: for hosted API customers we recommend doing a signed webhook with a service token; in Dedicated/Private you can enable an internal connector via VPC peering so the runtime talks to your endpoints over private network.
[00:02:58] Samir: do you have examples of signing / auth? we have strict egress rules.
[00:03:03] Alex: yes — we'll share our security docs. Redwood supports KMS integration for signing, and on Private we can configure TLS + mTLS to your services. also we have RBAC in the Console so only certain keys can call functions.
[00:03:16] Maya: what's the difference in latency between hosted function-calling and private connector?
[00:03:21] Priya: hosted webhooks usually add network latency — typical 30-120ms depending on destination. with Dedicated VPC connectors you see much lower latency because it's intra-region and private — sub-30ms added in optimized setups. actual numbers depend on your infra.
[00:03:35] Tom: that aligns with concerns — for checkout flows we need p95 under 300ms total for the call. is that achievable?
[00:03:42] Priya: yes, on Dedicated with optimized batching and prefix caching we've helped customers hit p95 < 200ms for structured generation + function call, but depends on sequence length and model. we'll propose a benchmark in the POC.
[00:03:54] Alex: quick aside on Optimize: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching windows and quantization profiles per workload to trade off cost vs latency. we'll include recommendations in the POC.
[00:04:04] Maya: show me how the Console maps the JSON to downstream action — like how do we monitor failures?
[00:04:09] Priya: switching to Console view — you can create an Integration route, attach a schema and function binding, and enable guards. here you see a request trace: model output, schema validation result, function invocation, and response. filters let you surface schema errors and set alerts.
[00:04:25] [00:04:25] Speaker 1: (typing) 
[00:04:28] Priya: also we have runtime guards — rate limits, token budgets, and a 'safe mode' that blocks any outputs that violate a safety regex or a DLP check before function call.
[00:04:38] Tom: what about versioning? we need to pin model versions so that changes don't break production.
[00:04:42] Alex: you can pin model versions per route, and rollouts are supported — canary then full. Console shows diffed schema behavior across model versions in logs so you can detect regressions.
[00:04:54] Maya: any guardrails for prompt drift? like if we change prompt templates across teams.
[00:04:58] Priya: yes, we recommend storing canonical prompts in the Console as templates; Optimize can flag quality regressions against your eval set if a new prompt causes schema failures or lower accuracy.
[00:05:08] Samir: let's talk security compliance quickly — SOC2 and key management.
[00:05:12] Alex: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations on Private). Audit logs are available in the Console and can be shipped to your SIEM via webhook/S3. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[00:05:26] Tom: good. we also have data residency concerns for EU customers; can you restrict a route to eu-west-1?
[00:05:32] Priya: yes per-route region pinning is supported; you can route traffic to region-specific clusters and set fallback policies.
[00:05:39] Maya: demo time — can you show a live structured-output example with a slightly messy input?
[00:05:44] Priya: sure — paste in a customer message: 'I need to change order 8342 — remove item 110 and set qty to 2 for item 112 and urgent because promo messed up' — hitting the structured endpoint now.
[00:05:58] [00:05:58] Priya: model returns JSON, Console shows schema validation: order_id:8342, items: [{id:110, qty:0}, {id:112, qty:2}], reason: 'promo error' — unexpected promo_code stripped. good.
[00:06:10] Priya: now trigger the bound function — you can see the webhook request and the response from Acme's staging endpoint (simulated). the call completed in 180ms.
[00:06:20] Maya: 180ms - that's promising. what was the model + network split?
[00:06:24] Priya: about 120ms model generation and 60ms network to the webhook.
[00:06:29] Tom: for high load, will you batch multiple messages into a single call? we have bursty traffic during sale windows.
[00:06:36] Alex: Redwood has workload-aware batching. Optimize can suggest batching windows based on your latency SLO. for order updates, we tend to use smaller batches or no batching to keep latency tight; for enrichment tasks we recommend larger batches.
[00:06:48] Samir: are there cost estimates for different approaches? e.g., hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[00:06:53] Alex: yes — Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing, Dedicated is reserved capacity — lower $/token at commit, and Private is licensed plus infra. we'll provide a cost model spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[00:07:05] [00:07:05] Speaker 2: faint echo 
[00:07:08] Maya: on guardrails — can we block outputs that request PII, like asking the model to return a credit card number?
[00:07:14] Priya: yes — DLP rules and regex-based blockers run before function call. you can also configure the route to redact fields automatically and send redaction events to your audit log.
[00:07:26] Tom: what's the POC timeline you typically see?
[00:07:29] Alex: typically 3-4 weeks: week 1 kickoff and access, week 2 benchmark + tune, week 3 evaluate results + security signoff, week 4 wrap and decision. flexible though.
[00:07:39] Maya: can you run a POC against our staging environment? we'll provide a test dataset of 5k messages.
[00:07:44] Priya: yes — we'll need webhook endpoints and a small IAM role or token. for VPC-based Private connectors we'll need network details — Samir, that part's on you.
[00:07:53] Samir: noted. i'll open a ticket for peering and send the CIDR blocks.
[00:07:57] Alex: terrific — next i want to show a failure pattern: when model returns ambiguous quantities.
[00:08:02] Priya: demo: ambiguous 'set qty to two or three' — Redwood will return a flagged response and either call a clarification function or create a task in your queue depending on config. sample config shown here.
[00:08:16] Maya: can we route those flagged responses to a human-in-the-loop tool?
[00:08:19] Priya: absolutely — we integrate with common ticketing tools or you can build a webhook to your triage service.
[00:08:24] [00:08:24] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) 
[00:08:26] Tom: any scale limits we should know? QPS per route?
[00:08:30] Alex: default rate limits are applied per-account; in Dedicated you get reserved throughput with autoscaling. we'll size the Dedicated pool based on your QPS and model choice during the POC.
[00:08:40] Maya: model selection — do you recommend a particular model for structured output? some of our prompts are long.
[00:08:45] Priya: depends — for long context (multi-turn order history), we advise a large-context model. Redwood's catalog highlights model tradeoffs; we'll recommend a quantized variant or a sharded KV cache strategy for long histories to keep costs down.
[00:08:59] Tom: could you summarize expected costs for our 5k message POC?
[00:09:03] Alex: estimate depends on chosen model and token counts; rough ballpark we'll send in the spreadsheet — includes model tokens, function-call overhead, and networking.
[00:09:11] Maya: let's talk troubleshooting — if function calls fail intermittently, do you have retry semantics?
[00:09:16] Priya: yes configurable retries with exponential backoff, and dead-lettering to your queue. the Console shows success/failure rates and exposes the raw request/response.
[00:09:26] Tom: can we get an export of logs to our Splunk?
[00:09:29] Alex: yes — audit logs and request logs can be exported via S3 or direct SIEM integration.
[00:09:35] [00:09:35] Speaker 2: (brief pause) 
[00:09:38] Maya: any gotchas for using structured output with multilingual inputs? we have customers in spanish.
[00:09:43] Priya: model choice matters; schema validation is language-agnostic but the model needs to map semantics correctly. we recommend running a small multilingual eval during POC. Optimize will flag regressions.
[00:09:55] Samir: networking specifics for Private — do you support private DNS and internal endpoint resolution?
[00:09:59] Alex: yes — on Private we can set up private DNS and endpoint discovery. we'll coordinate with your infra on peering and routing.
[00:10:07] Tom: ok wrapping up — what should we expect in the follow-up?
[00:10:10] Alex: action items as mentioned: pricing + SOW, security pack, schema templates, and proposed POC timeline. we'll schedule kickoff for week of 8/17.
[00:10:19] Maya: sounds good. a couple quick clarifying q's: will you need production data for accurate benchmarks?
[00:10:24] Priya: sample production-like traces are ideal but you can anonymize. for latency/cost metrics we prefer real token distributions.
[00:10:33] Tom: thanks, good session. quick note: please include contact for escalation if we hit an incident during POC.
[00:10:40] Alex: noted — i'll include our CSM & on-call SE contact in the follow-up.
[00:10:45] [00:10:45] Speaker 1: meeting ended

[00:10:50] Endnotes: shared items: link to schema templates (will be attached post-call), POC spreadsheet (pricing), security docs (SOC2 + KMS).
